new_statements.rule_in_words: The Tegali cluster (described through its Tagom/Rashad dialect) is analysed as a two-tone register language (H/L) whose tone carries tense marking; no modern first-hand source says anything about word stress or its position. The only stress remarks are Stevenson's 1950s ones, transmitted second-hand: Tucker & Bryan 1966 (ch. 18b, from Stevenson): 'Stress would also seem to have some importance, but has not been fully investigated'; Stevenson 1956/57: 47, 49 and 1964: 86 (via Bashir 2025): stress 'plays a marked role' and 'stress and vowel change also play a part in tense-formation' -- modern authors (Bashir 2025, Aldawi 2022/2025) reinterpret this prominence as H/L tone. No source gives a stress-placement rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Aldawi 2025: 73 adds 'The existence of lexical tone still needs to be checked' (tone so far shown only to be grammatical); Tucker & Bryan 1966 (from Stevenson) report three tone levels but no tonal doublets.
new_statements.domain_note: Verb roots in citation/paradigm forms (mono- and disyllabic bound roots with person prefixes); Tagom dialect (Rashad town/hills, Glottolog rash1248), speakers interviewed in Khartoum 2018-2019. Not Tingal/Kajakja itself.
new_statements.identity_note: ting1253 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry: ISO 639-3 CR 2010-011 (Persson & Hammarström, adopted 2011-05-18) merged Tingal [tie] into Tegali [ras] = tega1236 after a field check showed Tingal (= Kajakja/Kajaja, c. 520-2,100 speakers, Tegali Hills) is a dialect of the Tegali cluster; the only published mention of Tingal is hearsay in Stevenson 1956/57: 103. No source describes Tingal itself. The quoted statement describes Tagom (= Gom = Rashad-town dialect; Glottolog rash1248 'Rashad Town-Hills', a child of tega1236), a sister dialect within the classless Tegali cluster (Tagom, Tegali, Umale, Kajakja per Aldawi & Nashid 2018 after Blench 2013). Any catalog entry should be filed under tega1236 (Tegali), not under the retired code.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The chapter reports (after Stevenson 1956-57) three tone levels for the Tegali-Tagoi group with no tonal minimal pairs found, and says stress 'would also seem to have some importance' but was not investigated. No placement of word stress is given anywhere; the vowel section (sec. 1) only mentions 'subsidiary values.. in unstressed syllables' and that some of these 'are not confined to unstressed syllables'.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the authors flag that stress 'has not been fully investigated' and that tone examples are unmarked
new_statements.identity_note: Tingal [tie] was merged into Tegali [ras] by ISO 639-3 change request 2010-011 (adopted 2011); it is the Kajakja village dialect of the Tegali cluster. No work describes Tingal itself. Tucker & Bryan ch. 18b covers the Tegali-Tagoi (Rashad) group as a whole, second-hand from Stevenson 1956-57; the existing Aldawi 2022 statement is on Tagom (= Gom/Rashad dialect of Tegali, rash1248).

readall_conflicts: No disagreement on placement, because no source gives a placement. There is a mild tension in the literature on the Rashad group about whether the pitch contrasts are tone or stress: Tucker & Bryan 1966 (after Stevenson 1956-57) report three tone levels but no tonal doublets and say stress 'would also seem to have some importance'; Stevenson, as quoted second-hand by Bashir 2025 (pp. 43, 49, on the sister cluster Tagoi), doubted that tone plays a role 'apart from stress'; the modern sources (Aldawi 2022, 2025 on Tagom; Bashir 2025 on Tagoi) treat the languages as tonal with two register tones, Aldawi 2025 adding that 'the existence of lexical tone still needs to be checked'. None states where word stress falls.

sources.note: Para <5>, p. 6: 'Tagom is a tonal language with two register tones H/L which play a major role in the marking of the tense system'; present = L on root, past = H spreading to affixes. Syllable structure 'moderately complex'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent). Tagom = Gom = Rashad dialect of the Tegali cluster, sister dialect of Kajakja/Tingal.
